analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift and the complete one-hunk change map. The sole change passes stopStringScope into EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request alongside the checkpoint target (patch HEAD lines 249–250). No independently supported security regression is established by that argument addition. Existing surrounding behavior includes request-ID collision guards, context/overflow rejection, service/KV admission, scoped cache staging, cancellation-aware retirement, and resource transfer to the event pump. Cache scope is passed separately into translation (BASE 242), while the pump receives translated stop strings (BASE 934–938). No supplied change directly modifies encryption, attestation, serving authorization, token accounting, or disk-cache policy.
Integration must inspect the definition and initialization of stopStringScope and the corresponding translation change: determine whether it alters consumer-requested stopping, generated output exposure, or cache identity/reuse. Relevant contracts are A-001, TB-007, T-041 (authenticated account isolation and scoped cache reuse), T-007 (output integrity), and T-010 (termination/resource consumption). Trace the new argument through native request submission and pump stop processing, including any interaction with prefix checkpoints and retirement. Those implementations are outside this excerpt; the new scope's semantics cannot be verified here. The indexed model was considered, but only T-041 was supplied in full. No finding is inferred from missing dependency evidence.
